title: The last train
passage: The station clock was three minutes slow. Mara discovered this while watching the last train pull away with her suitcase on board. She still had her ticket, a sandwich, and the small brass key to a house she had never seen. The porter looked down the empty platform. "Well," he said, "at least your luggage knows where it is going."

title: At the repair bench
passage: There were six screws on the cloth, arranged in the order they had come out. Nina lifted the cover and found the trouble immediately: a loose wire, barely touching its terminal. She tightened it, checked the connection, and pressed the switch. The little fan started with a click. Her father leaned over the bench. "You kept the screws in order this time." She handed him the screwdriver. "I learned from your radio."

title: Before the bakery opens
passage: At five in the morning, the bakery was already warm. Luis tipped flour into the bowl while his sister weighed the butter. Outside, a delivery driver stacked empty crates beside the door. They had forty loaves to shape before the first customers arrived, and someone had used the order book to prop up a wobbly table.

title: A map in the drawer
passage:
The map had been folded so often that the river had split in two. Someone had drawn a pencil circle around a footbridge and written "Saturday, 10:30" in the margin. Ruth checked the date on the back: June 1986. She took it downstairs to her mother, who was peeling an apple at the kitchen table.

"Where did you find that?"

"Under the spare keys."

Her mother set down the knife and smiled. "Your father was late. I waited forty minutes."

"Did he have a good excuse?"

"No. But he brought two cups of coffee, and somehow they were still hot."

title: The borrowed telescope
passage: We carried the telescope up three flights of stairs because the lift was broken. On the roof, Ben unfolded a chart and tried to match it to the sky. I adjusted the tripod. For the first ten minutes, we looked at a bright window in the building across the street. Then a cloud moved, Ben turned the tube, and a pale, sharply outlined moon filled the lens. Neither of us said anything for a while.

title: Saturday at the market
passage: The flower seller wanted twelve pounds for the whole bucket. I only needed a few stems, but it was beginning to rain and she was packing up. We settled on eight. On the bus home, a woman asked if I was getting married. "No," I said, moving the bucket so she could sit down. "I was supposed to buy potatoes."
